newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Quaestor pays no dividend on 1996.
newsitem.headline: Quaestor pays no dividend on 1996.

text.p: Hungary's Quaestor Securities and Investment Rt decided not to pay dividend on its 1996 earnings, managing director Laszlo Somlai told Reuters on Monday after the company's annual general meeting.

Small investors, who acquired almost half of the company's shares in a public offering in December, would have been entitled for only a fractional dividend, for the very end of last year, Somlai said.
That was the reason why the shareholders agreed that Quaestor would not pay dividend for 1996, he said.
"But on the result of this year... there will be fairly substantial dividend, that is sure," he added.
On the 1995 earnings Quaestor did not pay dividend either.
Somlai said Quaestor boosted its after-tax profits to 94.3 million forints in 1996 from 40.8 million in 1995.
The company's turnover in government securities rose about fivefold, while the increase in stocks was sevenfold, he said.

He added that Quaestor's trading volume in Treasury bills reached 41.97 billion forints in 1996, in government bonds it amounted to 45.1 billion forints and in stocks traded on the Budapest Stock Exchange (BSE) to 1.8 billion forints.
Quaestor shares closed at 2,835 forints on the BSE on April 17.
